title: Friction stitchbook: probe anchors and quick-deploy proposals
content:
TL;DR:
This is a lightweight stitchbook of recurring runtime/UX friction reported by customers in the last 8 weeks, with three low-effort probe anchors (quick experiments) that shipping teams can pick up for fast impact. Goal: reduce noisy retries and observable token cost spikes for mid-market customers using hosted API and Dedicated tiers.

How this doc was assembled:
- Source signals: 24 support threads, 5 post-sales interviews, daily telemetry snapshots (latency percentiles + token churn), and two SRE on-call summaries.
- Prioritization heuristic: frequency x operational pain x engineering cost (low/medium/high). We only include items flagged as low or medium cost for quick deploy proposals.

Key themes (distilled):
1) Prefix cache misses causing token/regeneration cascades: customers with interactive chat flows report intermittent bursts where KV cache appears invalidated mid-session, prompting client retries.
2) Token accounting surprises: some customers think our per-request token charge increases when prompt concatenation patterns shift — often due to hidden system prompts or non-obvious metadata.
3) Variant fallback oscillation: when primary model hits capacity, automated fallback to a slightly different model sometimes alters response shape (formatting/trim) and triggers client-side retries.
4) Observability gaps: product teams see spikes but cannot map them to specific routes or customer API keys quickly.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
- Vignette A (customer: finance-SaaS): "Mid-conversation the bot started repeating itself and requests took 10x tokens — thought we were looped. We retried twice and then disabled the feature for a day."
- Vignette B (customer: developer-platform): "Fallback changed bullet formatting and our parser failed; we had to roll back to a cached response. Hard to diagnose which model did it."

Three probe anchors (recommended order):
Probe 1 — KV-cache-stability flag (low effort, quick rollback):
- What: Add a per-session stability score in trace logs and a soft flag in responses indicating "kv-cache-stable:true|false" for dedicated/hosted debug mode.
- Why: Makes it trivial for CS/engineers to correlate customer reports with cache invalidation without enabling full debug traces.
- Success signal: Reduction in repeat retries within 30 minutes for flagged sessions; support cases include the new flag and confirm correlation.
- Rough implementation notes: add small boolean to response envelope when prefix cache was reused for >=80% of tokens this request. Expose only in debug mode.

Probe 2 — Token-visibility shim in SDK (very low effort):
- What: SDK patch that emits a concise per-request token summary (prompt|completion|system) to console/log when debug enabled, plus opt-in metadata header for hosted API.
- Why: Customers repeatedly misattribute token increases. Visible breakdown reduces confusion and escalations.
- Success signal: Drop in token-accounting support tickets and faster CS TTR.
- Rough implementation notes: change only client SDKs (node/python) to avoid server-side rollout. Provide a sample snippet for customers.

Probe 3 — Fallback-consistency guard (medium effort):
- What: When our router triggers fallback to a different model family, attach a lightweight compatibility hint (formatting profile tag) and allow client-side opt-out or server side auto-normalizer to prefer structural parity.
- Why: Prevents client retries triggered by slight formatting/regression differences when capacity fallback occurs.
- Success signal: Reduced parser failures and fewer rollback incidents after fallback events.
- Rough implementation notes: add a string tag like "format:v2-compact" to response metadata; product and SDK teams to coordinate safe exposures.

Impact estimates (back-of-envelope):
- % of incidents covered by these probes: ~45% (from the filtered corpus of incidents labeled kernel:kv-cache|fallback|billing-visibility).
- Customer-seen TTR improvement (if probes succeed): median support time down from 6h -> 1.5h for these classes.
- Estimated engineering effort: Probe1: 3-5 engineer-days + 1 SRE review; Probe2: 1-2 engineer-days across SDK owners; Probe3: 1-2 weeks engineering + rollout coordination.

Engineering bridges (explicit handoffs):
- Serving-runtime: quick flag design review (Probe1) — owner: Marcus Li.
- SDK owners (node/python): implement Token-visibility shim (Probe2) — owner: Ava Patel.
- Routing/orchestration: evaluate format-tag schema and safe exposure (Probe3) — owner: Daniel Kim.

Observability / metric hooks to add: (small list)
- kv_cache_reuse_pct per-session histogram (expose via existing traces).
- fallback_format_mismatch counter (increment when format tag changes between rounds).
- dbg_token_breakdown_requested header count (to measure adoption of Probe2).

Quick deploy runbook (minimum viable rollout):
1) Ship SDK shim to a canary beta cohort (internal + 5 customers) — 1 week.
2) Add kv-cache-stable flag in hosted debug envelope behind a feature gate; enable for SRE traces and CS debug access — 4 days.
3) Test format-tag in routing path internally with synthetic load and one customer pilot — 2 weeks.

Open questions and risk notes:
- Privacy/compliance: ensure debug flags do not leak user content; only expose boolean/summary metadata, not token payloads. Legal review recommended if any customer data surfaces in traces.
- Billing surface exposure: token breakdown in SDK is informational; confirm it won’t be treated as a canonical billing statement by customers. Clarify in README.
- Behavioral regressions: format-tag normalizer must avoid changing semantics; product-owned test-suite for format parity required.

Next steps (short horizon):
- [Sophie] finalize probe specs and submit three short RFCs to eng teams (due 2026-05-14).
- [Marcus] review Probe1 feasibility and provide estimated API changes (due 2026-05-10).
- [Ava] prototype SDK shim and share example repo (due 2026-05-11).
- [Daniel] draft routing format-tag proposal and list integration points (due 2026-05-17).

Appendix: quick list of tickets to spin up (suggested titles)
- REQ: kv-cache-stability-flag + trace schema
- REQ: sdk-token-visibility-shim-node
- REQ: sdk-token-visibility-shim-python
- REQ: fallback-format-tagging-and-normalizer

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lean — meant to be a bridge doc between CS signals and fast engineering probes. Please comment on priority ordering and any missed low-effort wins.
- If you have a customer who would accept a short pilot for Probe2 (SDK shim), add them to collaborators and I'll reach out.

End of stitchbook.
